points.description: Correct final answer: the maximum possible number of elements of {P(a)+P(-a)} is 2 (answer 2 must be stated; other numbers such as 1 or 3 earn nothing here). Full marks also require a valid construction/verification of a P that attains 2 values (and that satisfies the equation).

levels.says: States 2 but gives no (or an unverified/incorrect) example attaining two values.

points.description: Proves P is bijective (injective and surjective) from the given condition, e.g. by choosing b so that the second factor or first factor structure forces P(b-P(a))=b-a-type relations, or by otherwise valid arguments. Note: guessing without proof earns nothing.

levels.says: Proves only injectivity or only surjectivity validly.

points.description: Proves P(-P(x)) = -x for all rational x (e.g. by substitution such as b=P(a) into the equation and using bijectivity/the factor analysis). Valid equivalent derivations accepted.

levels.says: Right identity stated and partial derivation with a gap in the case analysis of the two factors.

points.description: Characterises all solutions P (or otherwise derives enough structure) by correct case analysis of which factor vanishes, using P(-P(x))=-x and bijectivity; the characterisation is correct and complete (includes P(x)=x and P(x)=-x as solutions and the non-trivial ones).

levels.says: Finds some solutions (e.g. x and -x) and a partial structure, but characterisation incomplete or unproved.

points.description: Using the structure, proves that P(a)+P(-a) can take only finitely many values (at most 2), covering all solutions rigorously, not just the examples found.

levels.says: Finiteness shown only for a subfamily of solutions.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a proof of finiteness (not only guessed solutions) plus the answer 2 with a valid example reaching it. Part marks go to proved lemmas: bijectivity and P(-P(x))=-x, and to a correct partial classification. Guessing P without proving the lemmas earns only the answer/example credit; a wrong maximum earns no P1 marks.
rubric.answer_key: Answer: 2. Sketch: the equation says for every a,b, either P(b-P(a)) = P(b)-a or P(a+P(b-P(a))) = b. Use it to prove P is bijective, then P(-P(x)) = -x. Then analyse the factors to classify all P (identity and negation are solutions, with sum 0) and show P(a)+P(-a) takes at most two values over all solutions; a solution attaining two distinct values exists. Maximum number of elements = 2.
